question: Prostaglandin E1 (PGE1) infusion is used to keep the ductus arteriosus patent in neonates with duct-dependent cyanotic congenital heart disease until definitive surgical palliation or repair can be arranged.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is TRUE. PGE1 is a critical neonatal intervention for duct-dependent cyanotic CHD. The ductus arteriosus normally closes within 12-24 hours after birth; in lesions dependent on ductal flow for either pulmonary or systemic perfusion, pharmacological maintenance of the duct with PGE1 is essential as a bridge to definitive intervention.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. In lesions where pulmonary blood flow depends on the ductus (pulmonary atresia, critical pulmonary stenosis, tricuspid atresia with restricted pulmonary flow) or where systemic flow is duct-dependent, PGE1 maintains ductal patency and can be life-saving in the neonatal period. It is a bridge to surgery, not a cure.
